enumeratedValue.name: EQUAL_TO
enumeratedValue.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.

enumeratedValue.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN
enumeratedValue.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.

enumeratedValue.name: EQUAL_TO
enumeratedValue.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.

enumeratedValue.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN
enumeratedValue.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.

enumeratedValue.name: MASTER

enumeratedValue.name: LOCAL_SYNC

enumeratedValue.name: MASTER_SYNC
enumeratedValue.description: The master sync signal from submodule0 is used to force updates. This setting should not be used in submodule0 as it holds the FORCE OUTPUT signal to logic 0.

enumeratedValue.name: EXT_FORCE

enumeratedValue.name: EQUAL_TO
enumeratedValue.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period maintains this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.

enumeratedValue.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN
enumeratedValue.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWM_A output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.

cluster.name: FAULT[%s]
cluster.description: Array of registers: FCTRL, FCTRL2, FFILT, FSTS, FTST

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: FAULTx CPU interrupt requests disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: FAULTx CPU interrupt requests enabled.

enumeratedValue.name: NORMAL
enumeratedValue.description: Normal mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFPINx]. If neither FHALF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. The PWM outputs disabled by this fault input will not be re-enabled until the actual FAULTx input signal de-asserts since the fault input will combinationally disable the PWM outputs (as programmed in DISMAPn).

enumeratedValue.name: SAFE
enumeratedValue.description: Safe mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear and FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FHLAF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.

enumeratedValue.name: MANUAL
enumeratedValue.description: Manual fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. This is further controlled by FCTRL[FSAFE].

enumeratedValue.name: AUTOMATIC
enumeratedValue.description: Automatic fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are enabled when FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFLAGx]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.

enumeratedValue.name: LOGIC_0
enumeratedValue.description: A logic 0 on the fault input indicates a fault condition.

enumeratedValue.name: LOGIC_1
enumeratedValue.description: A logic 1 on the fault input indicates a fault condition.

enumeratedValue.description: No fault on the FAULTx pin.

enumeratedValue.name: DMAEN_0
enumeratedValue.description: DMA is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: DMAEN_1
enumeratedValue.description: DMA is enabled. DMA request asserts automatically when the values in the outer-set of buffered compare registers (UCOMP0/LCOMP0;UCOMP1/LCOMP1;UCOMP2/LCOMP2;UCOMP3/LCOMP3), initial registers(UINIT/LINIT) and modulus registers (UMOD/LMOD) are loaded into the inner-set of buffer and then LDOK is cleared automatically. After the completion of this DMA transfer, LDOK is set automatically, it ensures outer-set values can be loaded into inner-set which in turn triggers DMA again.

In this mode: (1)only when ENABLE=1, all counters (position/position difference/revolution/watchdog) can run, when ENABLE=0, all counters (position/position difference/revolution/watchdog) can't run. (2) the rising edge of PRESET input can initialize position/revolution/watchdog counters (position counter initialization also need referring to bit CTRL[REV]).

peripheral.name: CAN_MB0
peripheral.description: Flexible Data Rate CAN Message Buffer

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.name: DLC
field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR
field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.name: CODE
field.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.

field.name: ESI
field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.name: CODE
field.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.

field.name: ESI
field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.name: DLC
field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR

field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.name: EXT
field.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: STD
field.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: PRIO
field.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.

field.name: EXT
field.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: STD
field.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: PRIO
field.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.name: DLC
field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR
field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR
field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.name: CODE
field.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.

field.name: ESI
field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.name: CODE
field.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.

field.name: ESI
field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.name: DLC
field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR
field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.name: CODE
field.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.

field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR
field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.name: CODE
field.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.

field.name: ESI
field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.name: EXT
field.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: STD
field.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: PRIO
field.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.

field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.name: DLC
field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR
field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.name: STD
field.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: PRIO
field.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.name: DLC
field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR
field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.name: CODE
field.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.

field.name: ESI
field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.

field.name: ESI
field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.name: DLC
field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR
field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.name: EXT
field.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: STD
field.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: PRIO
field.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.

field.name: EXT
field.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: STD
field.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.name: DLC
field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR
field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.name: DLC
field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR
field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.name: CODE
field.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.

field.name: ESI
field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.name: EXT
field.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: STD
field.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: PRIO
field.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.

enumeratedValue.name: COUNTUP
enumeratedValue.description: Count up.

enumeratedValue.name: COUNTDOWN
enumeratedValue.description: Count down.

enumeratedValue.name: UNTIL_ROLLOVER
enumeratedValue.description: Count until roll over at $FFFF and then continue by re-initializing the counter from the LOAD register.

enumeratedValue.name: UNTIL_COMPARE
enumeratedValue.description: Count until compare, then re-initialize using the LOAD register. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, alternating values of COMP1 and COMP2 are used to generate successful comparisons. For example, the counter counts until a COMP1 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP2 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP1 value is reached, and so on.

enumeratedValue.name: REPEAT
enumeratedValue.description: Count repeatedly.

enumeratedValue.name: UNTIL_COMPARE
enumeratedValue.description: Count until compare and then stop. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, the counter re-initializes after reaching the COMP1 value, continues to count to the COMP2 value, and then stops.

enumeratedValue.name: COUNTUP
enumeratedValue.description: Count up.

enumeratedValue.name: COUNTDOWN
enumeratedValue.description: Count down.

enumeratedValue.name: UNTIL_ROLLOVER
enumeratedValue.description: Count until roll over at $FFFF and then continue by re-initializing the counter from the LOAD register.

enumeratedValue.name: UNTIL_COMPARE
enumeratedValue.description: Count until compare, then re-initialize using the LOAD register. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, alternating values of COMP1 and COMP2 are used to generate successful comparisons. For example, the counter counts until a COMP1 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP2 value is reached, re-initializes, counts until COMP1 value is reached, and so on.

enumeratedValue.name: REPEAT
enumeratedValue.description: Count repeatedly.

enumeratedValue.name: UNTIL_COMPARE
enumeratedValue.description: Count until compare and then stop. If counting up, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP1 value. If counting down, a successful compare occurs when the counter reaches a COMP2 value. When output mode $4 is used, the counter re-initializes after reaching the COMP1 value, continues to count to the COMP2 value, and then stops.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Timestamp Status Interrupt is enabled

field.name: RXSTSIE

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Receive Status Interrupt is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Receive Status Interrupt is enabled

field.name: FPEIE

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Frame Preemption Interrupt is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Frame Preemption Interrupt is enabled

field.name: MDIOIE

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: MDIO Interrupt is enabled

field.name: TJT
field.description: Transmit Jabber Timeout This bit indicates that the Transmit Jabber Timer expired which happens when the packet size exceeds 2,048 bytes (10,240 bytes when the Jumbo packet is enabled) and JD bit is reset in the MAC_CONFIGURATION register.

enumeratedValue.name: INACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: No Transmit Jabber Timeout

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Transmit Jabber Timeout occurred

field.name: NCARR
field.description: No Carrier When the DTXSTS bit is set in the MAC_OPERATION_MODE register, this bit indicates that the carrier signal from the PHY is not present at the end of preamble transmission.

enumeratedValue.name: INACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Carrier is present

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: No carrier

field.name: LCARR
field.description: Loss of Carrier When the DTXSTS bit is set in the MAC_OPERATION_MODE register, this bit indicates that the loss of carrier occurred during packet transmission, that is, the phy_crs_i signal was inactive for one or more transmission clock periods during packet transmission.

enumeratedValue.name: INACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Carrier is present

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Loss of carrier

field.name: EXDEF
field.description: Excessive Deferral When the DTXSTS bit is set in the MAC_OPERATION_MODE register and the DC bit is set in the MAC_CONFIGURATION register, this bit indicates that the transmission ended because of excessive deferral of over 24,288 bit times (155,680 in 1000/2500 Mbps mode or when Jumbo packet is enabled).

enumeratedValue.name: INACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: No Excessive deferral

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Excessive deferral

field.name: LCOL
field.description: Late Collision When the DTXSTS bit is set in the MAC_OPERATION_MODE register, this bit indicates that the packet transmission aborted because a collision occurred after the collision window (64 bytes including Preamble in MII mode; 512 bytes including Preamble and Carrier Extension in GMII mode).

enumeratedValue.name: INACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: No collision

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Late collision is sensed

field.name: EXCOL
field.description: Excessive Collisions When the DTXSTS bit is set in the MAC_OPERATION_MODE register, this bit indicates that the transmission aborted after 16 successive collisions while attempting to transmit the current packet.

enumeratedValue.name: INACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: No collision

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Excessive collision is sensed

field.name: RWT
field.description: Receive Watchdog Timeout This bit is set when a packet with length greater than 2,048 bytes is received (10, 240 bytes when Jumbo Packet mode is enabled) and the WD bit is reset in the MAC_CONFIGURATION register.

enumeratedValue.name: INACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: No receive watchdog timeout

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Receive watchdog timed out

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Power down is enabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Remote wake-up packet is received

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Skip Address Packet is enabled

field.name: CR
field.description: CSR Clock Range The CSR Clock Range selection determines the frequency of the MDC clock according to the CSR clock frequency used in your design: - 0000: CSR clock = 60-100 MHz; MDC clock = CSR clock/42 - 0001: CSR clock = 100-150 MHz; MDC clock = CSR clock/62 - 0010: CSR clock = 20-35 MHz; MDC clock = CSR clock/16 - 0011: CSR clock = 35-60 MHz; MDC clock = CSR clock/26 - 0100: CSR clock = 150-250 MHz; MDC clock = CSR clock/102 - 0101: CSR clock = 250-300 MHz; MDC clock = CSR clock/124 - 0110: CSR clock = 300-500 MHz; MDC clock = CSR clock/204 - 0111: CSR clock = 500-800 MHz; MDC clock = CSR clock/324 The suggested range of CSR clock frequency applicable for each value (when Bit 11 = 0) ensures that the MDC clock is approximately between 1.

field.name: NTC
field.description: Number of Trailing Clocks This field controls the number of trailing clock cycles generated on gmii_mdc_o (MDC) after the end of transmission of MDIO frame.

field.name: RDA
field.description: Register/Device Address These bits select the PHY register in selected Clause 22 PHY device.

field.name: PA
field.description: Physical Layer Address This field indicates which Clause 22 PHY devices (out of 32 devices) the MAC is accessing.

field.name: BTB
field.description: Back to Back transactions When this bit is set and the NTC has value greater than 0, then the MAC informs the completion of a read or write command at the end of frame transfer (before the trailing clocks are transmitted).

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Back to Back transactions disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Back to Back transactions enabled

field.name: PSE
field.description: Preamble Suppression Enable When this bit is set, the SMA suppresses the 32-bit preamble and transmits MDIO frames with only 1 preamble bit.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Preamble Suppression disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Preamble Suppression enabled

field.name: GD

field.name: RA
field.description: Register Address This field is valid only when C45E is set.

field.name: RCWE

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE

field.name: SA
field.description: Source Address When this bit is set, the MAC ADDRESS31[47:0] is used to compare with the SA fields of the received packet.

enumeratedValue.name: DA
enumeratedValue.description: Compare with Destination Address

enumeratedValue.name: SA
enumeratedValue.description: Compare with Source Address

field.name: AE
field.description: Address Enable When this bit is set, the address filter module uses the 32nd MAC address for perfect filtering.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Address is ignored

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Address is enabled

field.name: CNTRST
field.description: Counters Reset When this bit is set, all counters are reset.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Counters are not reset

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: All counters are reset

field.name: CNTSTOPRO
field.description: Counter Stop Rollover When this bit is set, the counter does not roll over to zero after reaching the maximum value.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Counter Stop Rollover is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Counter Stop Rollover is enabled

field.name: RSTONRD
field.description: Reset on Read When this bit is set, the MMC counters are reset to zero after Read (self-clearing after reset).

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Reset on Read is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Reset on Read is enabled

field.name: CNTFREEZ
field.description: MMC Counter Freeze When this bit is set, it freezes all MMC counters to their current value.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: MMC Counter Freeze is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: MMC Counter Freeze is enabled

field.name: CNTPRST
field.description: Counters Preset When this bit is set, all counters are initialized or preset to almost full or almost half according to the CNTPRSTLVL bit.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Counters Preset is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Counters Preset is enabled

field.name: CNTPRSTLVL
field.description: Full-Half Preset When this bit is low and the CNTPRST bit is set, all MMC counters get preset to almost-half value.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Full-Half Preset is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Full-Half Preset is enabled

field.name: UCDBC
field.description: Update MMC Counters for Dropped Broadcast Packets Note: The CNTRST bit has a higher priority than the CNTPRST bit.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Update MMC Counters for Dropped Broadcast Packets is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Update MMC Counters for Dropped Broadcast Packets is enabled

field.name: RXGBPKTIS
field.description: MMC Receive Good Bad Packet Counter Interrupt Status This bit is set when the rxpacketcount_gb counter reaches half of the maximum value or the maximum value.

enumeratedValue.name: INACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: MMC Receive Good Bad Packet Counter Interrupt Status not detected

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: MMC Receive Good Bad Packet Counter Interrupt Status detected

field.name: RXGBOCTIS
field.description: MMC Receive Good Bad Octet Counter Interrupt Status This bit is set when the rxoctetcount_gb counter reaches half of the maximum value or the maximum value.

enumeratedValue.name: INACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: MMC Receive Good Bad Octet Counter Interrupt Status not detected

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: MMC Receive Good Bad Octet Counter Interrupt Status detected

field.name: RXGOCTIS
field.description: MMC Receive Good Octet Counter Interrupt Status This bit is set when the rxoctetcount_g counter reaches half of the maximum value or the maximum value.

enumeratedValue.name: INACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: MMC Receive Good Octet Counter Interrupt Status not detected

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: MMC Receive Good Octet Counter Interrupt Status detected

field.name: RXBCGPIS
field.description: MMC Receive Broadcast Good Packet Counter Interrupt Status This bit is set when the rxbroadcastpackets_g counter reaches half of the maximum value or the maximum value.

enumeratedValue.name: INACTIVE

field.name: TXBCASTGB

register.name: MAC_TX_UNDERFLOW_ERROR_PACKETS
register.description: Tx Packets Aborted By Underflow Error

field.name: TXUNDRFLW
field.description: Tx Underflow Error Packets This field indicates the number of packets aborted because of packets underflow error.

field.name: TXSNGLCOLG
field.description: Tx Single Collision Good Packets This field indicates the number of successfully transmitted packets after a single collision in the half-duplex mode.

field.name: TXMULTCOLG
field.description: Tx Multiple Collision Good Packets This field indicates the number of successfully transmitted packets after multiple collisions in the half-duplex mode.

field.name: TXDEFRD
field.description: Tx Deferred Packets This field indicates the number of successfully transmitted after a deferral in the half-duplex mode.

field.name: TXLATECOL
field.description: Tx Late Collision Packets This field indicates the number of packets aborted because of late collision error.

field.name: TXEXSCOL
field.description: Tx Excessive Collision Packets This field indicates the number of packets aborted because of excessive (16) collision errors.

field.name: TXCARR
field.description: Tx Carrier Error Packets This field indicates the number of packets aborted because of carrier sense error (no carrier or loss of carrier).

field.name: TXOCTG
field.description: Tx Octet Count Good This field indicates the number of bytes transmitted, exclusive of preamble, only in good packets.

field.name: TXPKTG
field.description: Tx Packet Count Good This field indicates the number of good packets transmitted.

register.name: MAC_TX_EXCESSIVE_DEFERRAL_ERROR
register.description: Packets Aborted By Excessive Deferral Error

field.name: TXEXSDEF
field.description: Tx Excessive Deferral Error This field indicates the number of packets aborted because of excessive deferral error (deferred for more than two max-sized packet times).

field.name: TXPAUSE
field.description: Tx Pause Packets This field indicates the number of good Pause packets transmitted.

field.name: TXVLANG
field.description: Tx VLAN Packets Good This field provides the number of good VLAN packets transmitted.

field.name: TXOSIZG
field.description: Tx OSize Packets Good This field indicates the number of packets transmitted without errors and with length greater than the maxsize (1,518 or 1,522 bytes for VLAN tagged packets; 2000 bytes if enabled in S2KP bit of the CONFIGURATION register).

field.name: RXPKTGB
field.description: Rx Packets Count Good Bad This field indicates the number of good and bad packets received.

register.name: MAC_RX_OCTET_COUNT_GOOD_BAD
register.description: Bytes in Good and Bad Packets Received

field.name: RXOCTGB
field.description: Rx Octet Count Good Bad This field indicates the number of bytes received, exclusive of preamble, in good and bad packets.

field.name: RXOCTG
field.description: Rx Octet Count Good This field indicates the number of bytes received, exclusive of preamble, only in good packets.

field.name: RXBCASTG
field.description: Rx Broadcast Packets Good This field indicates the number of good broadcast packets received.

field.name: RXMCASTG
field.description: Rx Multicast Packets Good This field indicates the number of good multicast packets received.

field.name: RXCRCERR
field.description: Rx CRC Error Packets This field indicates the number of packets received with CRC error.

field.name: RXALGNERR
field.description: Rx Alignment Error Packets This field indicates the number of packets received with alignment (dribble) error.

field.name: RXRUNTERR
field.description: Rx Runt Error Packets This field indicates the number of packets received with runt (length less than 64 bytes and CRC error) error.

field.name: RXJABERR
field.description: Rx Jabber Error Packets This field indicates the number of giant packets received with length (including CRC) greater than 1,518 bytes (1,522 bytes for VLAN tagged) and with CRC error.

field.name: RXUNDERSZG
field.description: Rx Undersize Packets Good This field indicates the number of packets received with length less than 64 bytes, without any errors.

field.name: RXOVERSZG
field.description: Rx Oversize Packets Good This field indicates the number of packets received without errors, with length greater than the maxsize (1,518 bytes or 1,522 bytes for VLAN tagged packets; 2000 bytes if enabled in the S2KP bit of the MAC_CONFIGURATION register).

field.name: RX64OCTGB
field.description: Rx 64 Octets Packets Good Bad This field indicates the number of good and bad packets received with length 64 bytes, exclusive of the preamble.

field.description: Rx FIFO Overflow Packets This field indicates the number of missed received packets because of FIFO overflow.

register.name: MAC_RX_VLAN_PACKETS_GOOD_BAD
register.description: Good and Bad VLAN Packets Received

field.name: RXVLANPKTGB
field.description: Rx VLAN Packets Good Bad This field indicates the number of good and bad VLAN packets received.

field.name: RXWDGERR
field.description: Rx Watchdog Error Packets This field indicates the number of packets received with error because of watchdog timeout error (packets with a data load larger than 2,048 bytes (when JE and WD bits are reset in MAC_CONFIGURATION register), 10,240 bytes (when JE bit is set and WD bit is reset in MAC_CONFIGURATION register), 16,384 bytes (when WD bit is set in MAC_CONFIGURATION register) or the value programmed in the MAC_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT register).

field.name: RXRCVERR
field.description: Rx Receive Error Packets This field indicates the number of packets received with Receive error or Packet Extension error on the GMII or MII interface.

field.name: RXCTRLG
field.description: Rx Control Packets Good This field indicates the number of good control packets received.

field.name: TXLPIUSC
field.description: Tx LPI Microseconds Counter This field indicates the number of microseconds Tx LPI is asserted.

register.name: MAC_TX_LPI_TRAN_CNTR
register.description: Number of Times Tx LPI Asserted

field.name: TXLPITRC
field.description: Tx LPI Transition counter This field indicates the number of times Tx LPI Entry has occurred.

field.name: RXLPIUSC
field.description: Rx LPI Microseconds Counter This field indicates the number of microseconds Rx LPI is asserted.

register.name: MAC_RX_LPI_TRAN_CNTR

field.name: RXLPITRC
field.description: Rx LPI Transition counter This field indicates the number of times Rx LPI Entry has occurred.

field.name: RXIPV4HDRERRPKT

register.description: IPv4 Datagrams Received with No Payload

field.name: RXIPV4NOPAYPKT

field.name: RXIPV4FRAGPKT
field.description: RxIPv4 Fragmented Packets This field indicates the number of good IPv4 datagrams received with fragmentation.

field.name: FCIS
field.description: MMC Tx FPE Fragment Counter Interrupt status This bit is set when the Tx_FPE_Fragment_Cntr counter reaches half of the maximum value or the maximum value.

enumeratedValue.description: MMC Tx FPE Fragment Counter Interrupt status not detected

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: MMC Tx FPE Fragment Counter Interrupt status detected

enumeratedValue.name: INACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: MMC Tx Hold Request Counter Interrupt Status not detected

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: MMC Tx Hold Request Counter Interrupt Status detected

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE

field.description: Rx Packet Assembly OK Counter This field indicates the number of MAC frames that were successfully reassembled and delivered to MAC.

field.description: Rx FPE Fragment Counter This field indicates the number of additional mPackets received due to preemption Exists when at least one of the RX/TX MMC counters are enabled during FPE Enabled configuration.

register.name: MAC_L3_L4_CONTROL0
register.description: Layer 3 and Layer 4 Control of Filter 0

field.name: L3PEN0
field.description: Layer 3 Protocol Enable When this bit is set, the Layer 3 IP Source or Destination Address matching is enabled for IPv6 packets.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 3 Protocol is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 3 Protocol is enabled

field.name: L3SAM0
field.description: Layer 3 IP SA Match Enable When this bit is set, the Layer 3 IP Source Address field is enabled for matching.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 3 IP SA Match is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 3 IP SA Match is enabled

field.name: L3SAIM0
field.description: Layer 3 IP SA Inverse Match Enable When this bit is set, the Layer 3 IP Source Address field is enabled for inverse matching.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 3 IP SA Inverse Match is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 3 IP SA Inverse Match is enabled

field.name: L3DAM0
field.description: Layer 3 IP DA Match Enable When this bit is set, the Layer 3 IP Destination Address field is enabled for matching.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 3 IP DA Match is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 3 IP DA Match is enabled

field.name: L3DAIM0
field.description: Layer 3 IP DA Inverse Match Enable When this bit is set, the Layer 3 IP Destination Address field is enabled for inverse matching.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 3 IP DA Inverse Match is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 3 IP DA Inverse Match is enabled

field.name: L3HSBM0
field.description: Layer 3 IP SA Higher Bits Match IPv4 Packets: This field contains the number of lower bits of IP Source Address that are masked for matching in the IPv4 packets.

field.name: L3HDBM0
field.description: Layer 3 IP DA Higher Bits Match IPv4 Packets: This field contains the number of higher bits of IP Destination Address that are matched in the IPv4 packets.

field.name: L4PEN0
field.description: Layer 4 Protocol Enable When this bit is set, the Source and Destination Port number fields of UDP packets are used for matching.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 4 Protocol is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 4 Protocol is enabled

field.name: L4SPM0
field.description: Layer 4 Source Port Match Enable When this bit is set, the Layer 4 Source Port number field is enabled for matching.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 4 Source Port Match is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 4 Source Port Match is enabled

field.name: L4SPIM0
field.description: Layer 4 Source Port Inverse Match Enable When this bit is set, the Layer 4 Source Port number field is enabled for inverse matching.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 4 Source Port Inverse Match is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 4 Source Port Inverse Match is enabled

field.name: L4DPM0
field.description: Layer 4 Destination Port Match Enable When this bit is set, the Layer 4 Destination Port number field is enabled for matching.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 4 Destination Port Match is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 4 Destination Port Match is enabled

field.name: L4DPIM0
field.description: Layer 4 Destination Port Inverse Match Enable When this bit is set, the Layer 4 Destination Port number field is enabled for inverse matching.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 4 Destination Port Inverse Match is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 4 Destination Port Inverse Match is enabled

field.name: DMCHN0
field.description: DMA Channel Number When DMCHEN is set high, this field selects the DMA Channel number to which the packet passed by this filter is routed.

field.name: DMCHEN0
field.description: DMA Channel Select Enable When set, this bit enables the selection of the DMA channel number for the packet that is passed by this L3_L4 filter.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: DMA Channel Select is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: DMA Channel Select is enabled

field.name: L4SP0
field.description: Layer 4 Source Port Number Field When the L4PEN0 bit is reset and the L4SPM0 bit is set in the MAC_L3_L4_CONTROL0 register, this field contains the value to be matched with the TCP Source Port Number field in the IPv4 or IPv6 packets.

field.name: L4DP0
field.description: Layer 4 Destination Port Number Field When the L4PEN0 bit is reset and the L4DPM0 bit is set in the MAC_L3_L4_CONTROL0 register, this field contains the value to be matched with the TCP Destination Port Number field in the IPv4 or IPv6 packets.

field.description: Layer 3 IP DA Match Enable When this bit is set, the Layer 3 IP Destination Address field is enabled for matching.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 3 IP DA Match is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 3 IP DA Match is enabled

field.name: L3DAIM7
field.description: Layer 3 IP DA Inverse Match Enable When this bit is set, the Layer 3 IP Destination Address field is enabled for inverse matching.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 3 IP DA Inverse Match is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 3 IP DA Inverse Match is enabled

field.name: L3HSBM7
field.description: Layer 3 IP SA Higher Bits Match IPv4 Packets: This field contains the number of lower bits of IP Source Address that are masked for matching in the IPv4 packets.

field.name: L3HDBM7
field.description: Layer 3 IP DA Higher Bits Match IPv4 Packets: This field contains the number of higher bits of IP Destination Address that are matched in the IPv4 packets.

field.name: L4PEN7
field.description: Layer 4 Protocol Enable When this bit is set, the Source and Destination Port number fields of UDP packets are used for matching.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 4 Protocol is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 4 Protocol is enabled

field.name: L4SPM7
field.description: Layer 4 Source Port Match Enable When this bit is set, the Layer 4 Source Port number field is enabled for matching.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 4 Source Port Match is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 4 Source Port Match is enabled

field.name: L4SPIM7
field.description: Layer 4 Source Port Inverse Match Enable When this bit is set, the Layer 4 Source Port number field is enabled for inverse matching.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 4 Source Port Inverse Match is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 4 Source Port Inverse Match is enabled

field.name: L4DPM7
field.description: Layer 4 Destination Port Match Enable When this bit is set, the Layer 4 Destination Port number field is enabled for matching.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 4 Destination Port Match is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 4 Destination Port Match is enabled

field.name: L4DPIM7
field.description: Layer 4 Destination Port Inverse Match Enable When this bit is set, the Layer 4 Destination Port number field is enabled for inverse matching.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 4 Destination Port Inverse Match is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Layer 4 Destination Port Inverse Match is enabled

field.name: DMCHN7
field.description: DMA Channel Number When DMCHEN is set high, this field selects the DMA Channel number to which the packet passed by this filter is routed.

field.name: DMCHEN7
field.description: DMA Channel Select Enable When set, this bit enables the selection of the DMA channel number for the packet that is passed by this L3_L4 filter.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: DMA Channel Select is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: DMA Channel Select is enabled

field.name: L4SP7
field.description: Layer 4 Source Port Number Field When the L4PEN7 bit is reset and the L4SPM0 bit is set in the MAC_L3_L4_CONTROL0 register, this field contains the value to be matched with the TCP Source Port Number field in the IPv4 or IPv6 packets.

field.name: L4DP7
field.description: Layer 4 Destination Port Number Field When the L4PEN7 bit is reset and the L4DPM7 bit is set in the MAC_L3_L4_CONTROL0 register, this field contains the value to be matched with the TCP Destination Port Number field in the IPv4 or IPv6 packets.

field.name: L3A07
field.description: Layer 3 Address 0 Field When the L3PEN0 and L3SAM0 bits are set in the MAC_L3_L4_CONTROL0 register, this field contains the value to be matched with Bits[31:0] of the IP Source Address field in the IPv6 packets.

field.name: L3A17
field.description: Layer 3 Address 1 Field When the L3PEN0 and L3SAM0 bits are set in the MAC_L3_L4_CONTROL0 register, this field contains the value to be matched with Bits[63:32] of the IP Source Address field in the IPv6 packets.

field.name: L3A27
field.description: Layer 3 Address 2 Field When the L3PEN0 and L3SAM0 bits are set in the MAC_L3_L4_CONTROL0 register, this field contains the value to be matched with Bits[95:64] of the IP Source Address field in the IPv6 packets.

field.name: L3A37
field.description: Layer 3 Address 3 Field When the L3PEN0 and L3SAM0 bits are set in the MAC_L3_L4_CONTROL0 register, this field contains the value to be matched with Bits[127:96] of the IP Source Address field in the IPv6 packets.

field.name: COM
field.description: Command type. Indicates the register access type.

enumeratedValue.name: WRITE
enumeratedValue.description: Indicates a write operation

enumeratedValue.name: READ
enumeratedValue.description: Indicates a read operation

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: AOFF is not incremented automatically. Software should program the correct Address Offset for each access.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: AOFF is incremented by 1. Software should ensure not to cause a wrap condition. Byte wise read/write is not supported when auto increment is enabled.

field.name: DATA
field.description: This field contains data to read/write for Indirect address access associated with MAC_INDIR_ACCESS_CTRL register.

field.name: TSENA
field.description: Enable Timestamp When this bit is set, the timestamp is added for Transmit and Receive packets.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Timestamp is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Timestamp is enabled

field.name: TSCFUPDT
field.description: Fine or Coarse Timestamp Update When this bit is set, the Fine method is used to update system timestamp.

enumeratedValue.name: COARSE
enumeratedValue.description: Coarse method is used to update system timestamp

enumeratedValue.name: FINE
enumeratedValue.description: Fine method is used to update system timestamp

field.name: TSINIT
field.description: Initialize Timestamp When this bit is set, the system time is initialized (overwritten) with the value specified in the MAC_System_Time_Seconds_Update and MAC_System_Time_Nanoseconds_Update registers.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Timestamp is not initialized

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Timestamp is initialized

field.name: TSUPDT
field.description: Update Timestamp When this bit is set, the system time is updated (added or subtracted) with the value specified in MAC_System_Time_Seconds_Update and MAC_System_Time_Nanoseconds_Update registers.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Timestamp is not updated

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Timestamp is updated

field.name: TSADDREG
field.description: Update Addend Register When this bit is set, the content of the Timestamp Addend register is updated in the PTP block for fine correction.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Addend Register is not updated

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Addend Register is updated

field.name: PTGE
field.description: Presentation Time Generation Enable When this bit is set the Presentation Time generation will be enabled.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Presentation Time Generation is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Presentation Time Generation is enabled

field.name: TSENALL
field.description: Enable Timestamp for All Packets When this bit is set, the timestamp snapshot is enabled for all packets received by the MAC.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Timestamp for All Packets disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Timestamp for All Packets enabled

field.name: TSCTRLSSR
field.description: Timestamp Digital or Binary Rollover Control When this bit is set, the Timestamp Low register rolls over after 0x3B9A_C9FF value (that is, 1 nanosecond accuracy) and increments the timestamp (High) seconds.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Timestamp Digital or Binary Rollover Control is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Timestamp Digital or Binary Rollover Control is enabled

field.name: TSVER2ENA
field.description: Enable PTP Packet Processing for Version 2 Format When this bit is set, the IEEE 1588 version 2 format is used to process the PTP packets.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: PTP Packet Processing for Version 2 Format is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: PTP Packet Processing for Version 2 Format is enabled

field.name: TSIPENA
field.description: Enable Processing of PTP over Ethernet Packets When this bit is set, the MAC receiver processes the PTP packets encapsulated directly in the Ethernet packets.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Processing of PTP over Ethernet Packets is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Processing of PTP over Ethernet Packets is enabled

field.name: TSIPV6ENA
field.description: Enable Processing of PTP Packets Sent over IPv6-UDP When this bit is set, the MAC receiver processes the PTP packets encapsulated in IPv6-UDP packets.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Processing of PTP Packets Sent over IPv6-UDP is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Processing of PTP Packets Sent over IPv6-UDP is enabled

field.name: TSIPV4ENA
field.description: Enable Processing of PTP Packets Sent over IPv4-UDP When this bit is set, the MAC receiver processes the PTP packets encapsulated in IPv4-UDP packets.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Processing of PTP Packets Sent over IPv4-UDP is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Processing of PTP Packets Sent over IPv4-UDP is enabled

field.name: TSEVNTENA
field.description: Enable Timestamp Snapshot for Event Messages When this bit is set, the timestamp snapshot is taken only for event messages (SYNC, Delay_Req, Pdelay_Req, or Pdelay_Resp).

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Timestamp Snapshot for Event Messages is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Timestamp Snapshot for Event Messages is enabled

field.name: TSMSTRENA
field.description: Enable Snapshot for Messages Relevant to Master When this bit is set, the snapshot is taken only for the messages that are relevant to the master node.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Snapshot for Messages Relevant to Master is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Snapshot for Messages Relevant to Master is enabled

field.name: SNAPTYPSEL
field.description: Select PTP packets for Taking Snapshots These bits, along with Bits 15 and 14, decide the set of PTP packet types for which snapshot needs to be taken.

field.name: TSENMACADDR
field.description: Enable MAC Address for PTP Packet Filtering When this bit is set, the DA MAC address (that matches any MAC Address register) is used to filter the PTP packets when PTP is directly sent over Ethernet.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: MAC Address for PTP Packet Filtering is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: MAC Address for PTP Packet Filtering is enabled

field.name: CSC
field.description: Enable checksum correction during OST for PTP over UDP/IPv4 packets When this bit is set, the last two bytes of PTP message sent over UDP/IPv4 is updated to keep the UDP checksum correct, for changes made to origin timestamp and/or correction field as part of one step timestamp operation.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: checksum correction during OST for PTP over UDP/IPv4 packets is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: checksum correction during OST for PTP over UDP/IPv4 packets is enabled

field.name: ESTI
field.description: External System Time Input When this bit is set, the MAC uses the external 64-bit reference System Time input for the following: - To take the timestamp provided as status - To insert the timestamp in transmit PTP packets when One-step Timestamp or Timestamp Offload feature is enabled.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: External System Time Input is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: External System Time Input is enabled

field.name: TXTSSTSM
field.description: Transmit Timestamp Status Mode When this bit is set, the MAC overwrites the earlier transmit timestamp status even if it is not read by the software.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Transmit Timestamp Status Mode is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Transmit Timestamp Status Mode is enabled

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: AV 802.1AS Mode is disabled

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: AV 802.1AS Mode is enabled

field.name: SNSINC
field.description: Sub-nanosecond Increment Value This field contains the sub-nanosecond increment value, represented in nanoseconds multiplied by 2^8.

field.name: SSINC
field.description: Sub-second Increment Value The value programmed in this field is accumulated every clock cycle (of clk_ptp_i) with the contents of the sub-second register.

field.name: TSS
field.description: Timestamp Second The value in this field indicates the current value in seconds of the System Time maintained by the MAC.

field.name: TSSS
field.description: Timestamp Sub Seconds The value in this field has the sub-second representation of time, with an accuracy of 0.

field.name: TSS
field.description: Timestamp Seconds The value in this field is the seconds part of the update.

field.name: TSSS
field.description: Timestamp Sub Seconds The value in this field is the sub-seconds part of the update.

field.name: ADDSUB
field.description: Add or Subtract Time When this bit is set, the time value is subtracted with the contents of the update register.

enumeratedValue.name: ADD
enumeratedValue.description: Add time

enumeratedValue.name: SUB
enumeratedValue.description: Subtract time

field.name: TSAR
field.description: Timestamp Addend Register This field indicates the 32-bit time value to be added to the Accumulator register to achieve time synchronization.

field.name: TSHWR
field.description: Timestamp Higher Word Register This field contains the most-significant 16-bits of timestamp seconds value.

field.name: TSSOVF
field.description: Timestamp Seconds Overflow When this bit is set, it indicates that the seconds value of the timestamp (when supporting version 2 format) has overflowed beyond 32'hFFFF_FFFF.

enumeratedValue.name: INACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Timestamp Seconds Overflow status not detected

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Timestamp Seconds Overflow status detected

field.name: TSTARGT0
field.description: Timestamp Target Time Reached When set, this bit indicates that the value of system time is greater than or equal to the value specified in the MAC_PPS0_Target_Time_Seconds and MAC_PPS0_Target_Time_Nanoseconds registers.

enumeratedValue.name: INACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Timestamp Target Time Reached status not detected

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Timestamp Target Time Reached status detected

field.name: AUXTSTRIG
field.description: Auxiliary Timestamp Trigger Snapshot This bit is set high when the auxiliary snapshot is written to the FIFO.

enumeratedValue.name: INACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Auxiliary Timestamp Trigger Snapshot status not detected

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Auxiliary Timestamp Trigger Snapshot status detected

field.name: TSTRGTERR0
field.description: Timestamp Target Time Error This bit is set when the latest target time programmed in the MAC_PPS0_Target_Time_Seconds and MAC_PPS0_Target_Time_Nanoseconds registers elapses.

enumeratedValue.name: INACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Timestamp Target Time Error status not detected

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Timestamp Target Time Error status detected

enumeratedValue.name: INACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Timestamp Target Time Error status not detected

enumeratedValue.name: INACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Timestamp Target Time Reached for Target Time PPS3 status not detected

enumeratedValue.description: Tx Timestamp Status Interrupt status not detected

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE

enumeratedValue.name: INT_ST
enumeratedValue.description: Target Time registers are programmed for generating the interrupt event and starting or stopping the PPS0 output signal generation

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Head-Of-Line Blocking due to Frame Size detected

field.name: HLBS

field.name: RADV

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE
